message.content:
Lions (Panthera leo) belong to the family **Felidae** in the order **Carnivora**, while zebras (Equus quagga) belong to the family **Equidae** in the order **Perissodactyla**.  
Because those two orders diverged very early in mammalian evolution, the most recent common ancestor of a lion and a zebra is not a specific species but a small, insect‑eating mammal that lived roughly **70–80 million years ago** during the late Cretaceous/early Paleogene.  

That ancestor would have been a member of the early placental mammals (Eutheria) that gave rise to the two distinct lineages that eventually became the modern carnivores and odd‑toed ungulates. In other words, the last common ancestor of lions and zebras is a generic early placental mammal that existed before the split between the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla.
message.reasoning:
The user asks: "What is the common ancestor of lion and zebra?" They want a biological answer. We can provide a general answer: The common ancestor of lions (Panthera leo) and zebras (Equus quagga) is a mammalian ancestor from the order Carnivora for lions and order Perissodactyla for zebras. But they share a common ancestor at the level of the class Mammalia, perhaps the last common ancestor of all placental mammals. The last common ancestor of lions and zebras would be the last common ancestor of the families Felidae (cats) and Equidae (horses). That ancestor would be a member of the order Carnivora? Wait, lions are in order Carnivora, family Felidae. Zebras are in order Perissodactyla, family Equidae. So the last common ancestor of lions and zebras would be at the level of the class Mammalia, specifically the last common ancestor of the orders Carnivora and Perissodactyla. That ancestor would be a mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago, likely a small, insectivorous mammal. The last common ancestor of all placental mammals is older (~100-120 million years ago). So we can say: The last common ancestor of lions and zebras is a small, insectivorous mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago, belonging to the group of early placental mammals. Or we can mention the last common ancestor of the families Felidae and Equidae is a mammal that lived around 70-80 million years ago. Provide a general answer.
